title: Hello World
intro: Today you teach the computer to TALK — your very first magic word!

steps.title: Meet print — the computer's voice
steps.text: print is a magic word that makes the computer say things on the screen. You type print, then ( ), and inside the ( ) you put words in quotes.

steps.title: Your turn! Make it say YOUR words
steps.text: Change the words inside the quotes and press Run. The computer will say whatever you put between the " " marks.
steps.funFact: The " " marks are called quotes — they tell the computer 'these are words, not magic commands!'

steps.title: Two things at once
steps.text: You can put lots of things inside print, separated by commas. The computer puts a space between them!

steps.title: Make art with print
steps.text: You can even draw pictures with print! Every line becomes a line on the screen.
steps.funFact: This is called ASCII art — pictures made only of keyboard letters!

title: Name Boxes
intro: Today you teach the computer to REMEMBER things in little boxes!

steps.title: First — remember print?
steps.text: Last week you taught the computer to TALK with print! Press Run and hear it say hello again.

steps.title: Ready for something new?
steps.text: Super! Now today we learn how to make the computer REMEMBER things — in magic boxes with names on them!

steps.title: What is a variable?
steps.text: A variable is a box with a name on it. You put something inside — a word or a number — and the computer remembers it for later.

steps.title: Making a word box
steps.text: Type name = "Ava" to make a box called name with the word Ava inside. Then print(name) OPENS the box!
steps.funFact: No quotes around 'name' when you print it — that would print the word 'name', not what's inside!

steps.title: Number boxes (no quotes!)
steps.text: Numbers don't need quotes. Try age = 5 — no " " marks. The computer knows 5 is a number.
steps.visual:
age = 5       ← no quotes for numbers
name = "Ava"  ← quotes for words

steps.title: Two boxes together
steps.text: Make a hero and a power box, then print them in the same sentence. You can use as many boxes as you like!

steps.title: Change a box!
steps.text: You can put something NEW in the box any time. The old thing gets replaced.
steps.funFact: When you put something new in the box, the old one is gone forever — like clearing a toy chest!

mission.brief: Make a box called hero AND a box called power, then print them.

title: Joining Words
intro: Today you stick words together to make funny sentences and birthday cards!

steps.title: Remember boxes?
steps.text: Last week you made BOXES! Remember putting your name inside? Press Run and watch!

steps.title: Now — stick words together!
steps.text: Wonderful! Today we learn two magic signs that STICK words together to make bigger sentences.

steps.title: The + sign glues words
steps.text: The + sign sticks two words into one. It does NOT add a space — you have to put the space yourself inside the quotes.

steps.title: Glue a word AND a box
steps.text: You can glue a word to the stuff inside a box. Super handy for greeting people!

steps.title: Comma adds a space for you
steps.text: If you use a COMMA instead of +, the computer puts a space between them for you. Easier!

steps.title: Repeat with *
steps.text: The * sign REPEATS a word that many times! Great for silly stuff.
steps.funFact: This works with emojis too! Try print("⭐" * 10)

steps.title: Make a birthday card
steps.text: Put it all together — a birthday card for someone you love!

mission.brief: Join your name with Hello using +

title: Making Choices
intro: Today the computer learns to make CHOICES — like a little brain of its own!

steps.title: Remember + and comma?
steps.text: Last week you joined words with + and commas! Remember? Press Run.

steps.title: Now — teach the computer to CHOOSE
steps.text: Perfect! Today the computer learns to make choices by itself. Like a little brain!

steps.title: What is if?
steps.text: if is a magic word that CHECKS something. If the check is true, the computer does what's inside. If not — it skips it!
steps.visual:
if it's raining: take an umbrella
if you're hungry: eat a snack

steps.title: if in Python
steps.text: Watch this! Change score to 2 and run again — see what happens?
steps.funFact: The > sign means "bigger than". So 10 > 5 is TRUE. But 2 > 5 is FALSE.

steps.title: The 4-space secret
steps.text: Did you spot the 4 spaces before print? That tells the computer this line is INSIDE the if. It's like a secret room!

steps.title: else — the backup plan
steps.text: else means 'if the check is NOT true, do THIS instead'. Now the computer always says something!

steps.title: The treasure game
steps.text: Change score to different numbers and press Run — see when you win and when you don't!

mission.brief: Make an if that prints 'win' when score is 10.

title: Loops
intro: Today the computer learns to do things AGAIN AND AGAIN — like magic!

steps.title: Remember if and else?
steps.text: Last week you taught the computer to CHOOSE! Press Run and remember!

steps.title: Now — LOOPS!
steps.text: Amazing! Today you teach the computer to REPEAT things. This is called a LOOP!

steps.title: What is a loop?
steps.text: A loop does the same thing many times. Like walking in circles, or clapping your hands 5 times!

steps.title: for ... in range(5)
steps.text: This magic line says: 'do the stuff inside 5 times!' The inside must be indented (4 spaces) like with if.
steps.funFact: range(5) makes the numbers 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 — that's 5 numbers total!

steps.title: A unicorn parade!
steps.text: Change the number in range to any amount you like!
steps.pre:
for i in range(6):
    print("🦄 Unicorn!")

steps.title: Use the counter
steps.text: The letter i (or whatever you call it) is the counter — it changes each time through the loop!
steps.pre:
for n in range(5):
    print("Number:", n)

steps.title: Count down and blast off!
steps.text: range(5, 0, -1) means count from 5 down to 1!

mission.brief: Print the word 'yay' three times with a loop.

title: Lists
intro: Today you learn LISTS — a magic box that holds LOTS of things in a line!

steps.title: Remember loops?
steps.text: Last week you made LOOPS! Press Run and watch the stars appear!

steps.title: Now — LISTS!
steps.text: Wow! Today you learn LISTS — a BIG box that holds many things in order!

steps.title: What is a list?
steps.text: A list is one box with lots of things inside, in a line. Like a line of toys on a shelf!

steps.title: Making a list
steps.text: Use SQUARE brackets [ ] and put things inside, separated by commas.

steps.title: Get ONE thing with its spot number
steps.text: pets[0] gets the FIRST one. Why 0? Because computers count starting from 0!
steps.visual:
pets[0] → cat
pets[1] → dog
pets[2] → unicorn
steps.funFact: In the computer world, FIRST is 0! It feels strange at first but you'll get used to it. 🙂

steps.title: Try spot 1 and 2!
steps.text: Change the number in the brackets to 1 or 2 and press Run!

steps.title: Loop through the whole list
steps.text: Combine lists with loops — go through each thing in order!

mission.brief: Make a list of 3 animals and print the first one.

title: Chat with Pixi
intro: Today the computer ASKS YOU questions — real chat with Pixi!

steps.title: Remember lists?
steps.text: Last week you made LISTS! Remember your pet shop? Press Run!

steps.title: Now — the computer asks YOU!
steps.text: Fantastic! Today the computer asks YOU questions — and waits for your answer!

steps.title: What is input()?
steps.text: input() shows a question and waits for you to type an answer. Then it remembers what you typed!
steps.visual:
You: name? 🤔
You type: Ava
Computer: remembers "Ava"

steps.title: Ask and remember
steps.text: Save the answer in a box, then use it! A little pop-up will appear for you to type in.
steps.pre:
name = input("What's your name? ")
print("Hello,", name)

steps.title: Make Pixi react to your answer
steps.text: Ask about a favourite thing — Pixi will reply!
steps.pre:
color = input("Favourite colour? ")
print("I love", color, "too!")

steps.title: A mini chat program
steps.text: Ask two questions and put the answers together!
steps.pre:
name = input("Name? ")
food = input("Favourite food? ")
print(name, "loves", food, "! 🍕")

mission.brief: Use input() to ask a name, then print a greeting.

title: Magic Words
intro: Today YOU teach the computer a brand new magic word — made by you!

steps.title: Remember input()?
steps.text: Last week Pixi ASKED you questions with input! Remember?

steps.title: Now — invent YOUR OWN magic word!
steps.text: Perfect! Today you teach the computer a BRAND NEW magic word — one that YOU invent!

steps.title: What is a function?
steps.text: A function is YOUR OWN magic word. You teach the computer what it does ONCE, then use it as many times as you like!
steps.visual:
def say_hi():         ← teach the word
    print("Hi there!")

say_hi()              ← use it!
say_hi()              ← use it again!

steps.title: Teach your first magic word
steps.text: def means 'DEFINE this new word'. Everything inside (4 spaces!) is what the word does.
steps.pre:
def say_hi():
    print("Hi there! 👋")

say_hi()
say_hi()
steps.funFact: You just wrote your first REAL program — the kind big kid programmers write!

steps.title: Give your magic word an input
steps.text: Put a word inside the ( ) when you teach it — then use that word inside!
steps.pre:
def greet(who):
    print("Hello " + who + "!")

greet("Ava")
greet("Pixi")
greet("Mom")

steps.title: Your own superpower!
steps.text: Make a magic word that gives someone a superpower!
steps.pre:
def superpower(hero, power):
    print(hero, "can", power, "✨")

superpower("Dragon", "fly")
superpower("Pixi", "code")

mission.brief: Write a def and call it twice!
